ask: Build the machine-load brake as a standing part of claude-settings, on every device that installs it (Windows and Mac, no admin): at the moment a lane is about to start, the guard reads the machine's load once and sets how many lanes may run.
note: Rulings, Oct 21: every device that installs claude-settings, storage as well as CPU and memory; accurate; cheaper than the problem (no watcher, no timer, no per-tool-call reading, no log of its own). Oct 22: no lane count and no claude process count. Landed in #562 (main 1842e56): memory and disk as shares, CPU from a 200 ms sample, busy refuses background spawns and Workflows. Session question 3, Oct 22: it refused every lane (CPU 87-94%, 35 claude processes). Correction, Oct 22: the advisor's reason 'this app has no background setting, so left out means foreground' was a guess and false; the session read claude.exe 2.1.308.0, and every Agent lane in this app runs in the background. Advice taken: keep the behaviour, fix the reason. In #564 (CI running Oct 23): a left-out or false run_in_background passes busy; CPU counts only with memory over 75%; so in this app busy slows only Workflows and explicit background calls, and full (memory over 95% or little disk) stops every lane. Mac findings, Oct 22, checked at 1842e56: disk is read as a percent, so on the 926 GB disk busy fires under about 139 GB free (it held lanes at 119 GB); Mac CPU uses the load average, which read 100% busy during Spotlight indexing while top showed about half idle. Ruling, Oct 23: disk busy under the smaller of 10% of the disk and 15 GB free, full under the smaller of 5% and 5 GB. Ruling, Oct 23 (replaced Oct 25): 2-second CPU sample on every platform, after a Mac lane read 100% busy against top's 24% idle. Finding, Oct 23 02:30 (advisor measured): 17 idle Claude Desktop CLI processes each burn about one core (CPU 93%, memory 72%); the brake reads that right, the load is real (c40). The live brake (at 1842e56) refuses even run_in_background false, likely because this app's Agent tool has no such field and the call arrives without it (cause unknown, not checked); #564 lets a left-out field pass and counts CPU only with memory over 75%, so once installed, Agent lanes pass at today's load and only Workflows wait. Landed, checked at claude-settings f463787 (main, Oct 25): #565 (brake reads the machine) put disk in GB against the smaller of a share and a cap, and CPU from ticks; #569 waited for a tick change before giving up a CPU read. Your ruling, Oct 25: CPU dropped (a short sample is noise; memory and disk are what stall a machine). #572 (brake drops the CPU reading) built it: the brake now reads memory and disk only; the decision machine-load-brake is rewritten to match. The Oct 23 two-second-sample ruling is replaced by this one.
title: Machine-load brake: every session paces its lanes to the device's real load
why: Your idea, Oct 20, widened Oct 21: when the machine is loaded, sessions slow down; when it has room, more lanes can run. Incidents: the 15 spinning claude.exe workers of Oct 19, the q_max load report, and the Windows RAM climb to about 98% of Oct 21. Your caution, Oct 21: measuring and logging have cost more than the problem before.
